meta.project_name: Responsive browser mode and agent-spawned device windows
meta.activation_reason: The user started the plan on pi-gna's ATP page.

T01_spike_emulation.title: Spike CDP emulation and detached windows, write the design
T01_spike_emulation.instruction:
Goal: ground the responsive-browser design in evidence from the real Electron 44 app, then write it down so every later node builds the same thing.

Steps:
1. Read docs/DESIGN.md (Browser M2) and the files named in context.
2. Write a throwaway harness (scripts/ or a temp file, deleted or kept small and documented afterwards) that creates a WebContentsView in persist-style session, attaches webContents.debugger, and measures each assumption on a fixture page that reports innerWidth/innerHeight, devicePixelRatio, matchMedia('(max-width: 480px)'), matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)'), navigator.userAgent and navigator.maxTouchPoints:
   a. Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride {width,height,deviceScaleFactor,mobile,screenWidth,screenHeight} applied once persists across navigations, reloads and a cross-origin navigation of the same tab; note if it must be re-applied (render-process-gone, devtools open/close).
   b. Emulation.setUserAgentOverride with userAgentMetadata and Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled: confirm the HTTP request User-Agent and Sec-CH-UA-Mobile header seen by a local http server (not just navigator.userAgent) match, including on reload.
   c. Fit-to-pane: when the emulated viewport is larger than the pane, compare (i) the `scale` parameter of setDeviceMetricsOverride with the native view sized to w*scale, versus (ii) leaving scale=1 and clipping/scrolling. Verify real OS mouse input and the annotate picker (src/main/browser/page-scripts.ts) still hit the right element under the chosen approach, and that CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent coordinates stay in emulated CSS pixels.
   d. Page.captureScreenshot dimensions with deviceScaleFactor 1/2/3 and with the window hidden/occluded.
   e. Whether webContents.openDevTools({mode:'detach'}) coexists with the attached debugger.
   f. Detached windows: create a second BrowserWindow with useContentSize at an exact content size, setAspectRatio, showInactive; move or create a WebContentsView in it; confirm the real device pixel ratio is the display's (so DPR must be emulated) and that CDP screenshots and input work while the window is not focused.
3. Write docs/RESPONSIVE_BROWSER.md recording: measured results (with the numbers), the chosen mechanism for each of a-f and why, the ViewportSpec shape (width, height, dpr, mobile, touch, userAgent profile id, label), the preset list (Responsive, Laptop 1440x900, Desktop 1920x1080, iPhone 15 393x852@3, iPhone SE 375x667@2, Pixel 8 412x915@2.625, iPad 820x1180@2, plus Custom), limits (e.g. 200..3840 per edge, dpr 1..4, max 4 agent windows per session), who may change a viewport (user and agent; no approval needed, it is not a navigation), and an ordered interface list for the later nodes. Flag anything that contradicts the plan so the orchestrator can replan.

Deliverables: docs/RESPONSIVE_BROWSER.md and any kept harness script. No product code changes in this node.

Acceptance: every assumption a-f has a measured yes/no (or a documented alternative) in the doc; the doc names the exact CDP calls and Electron APIs to use.
T01_spike_emulation.context: Project: pi-gna (Electron 44 desktop UI for the pi coding agent, macOS; repo /Users/manuelcecchetto/Code/personal/pi-gna). Read docs/DESIGN.md '## Browser (M2)' first. Existing browser code: src/main/browser/manager.ts (BrowserManager: one WebContentsView per tab in partition persist:pigna-browser; applyLayout() pins the active view to the DOM pane rect the renderer reports via browser:layout, scaled by the app zoom factor), src/main/browser/agent.ts (BrowserAgent behind POST /browser; input and screenshots go through CDP webContents.debugger, attached lazily by the local cdp() helper, because capturePage/sendInputEvent need composited frames), src/shared/browser.ts (BrowserState, AgentAction, AgentResult, pure helpers + browser.test.ts), src/shared/ipc.ts + src/preload/index.ts (IPC channels), src/renderer/src/components/BrowserPane.tsx (tab strip, toolbar, viewport div), src/renderer/src/lib/tools.ts (tool-call labels), resources/browser-extension.ts (pi extension registering browser_* tools; imports src/shared/browser.ts directly). Feature goal: a Codex-app-style responsive mode. The USER gets a Dimensions toolbar (presets, width x height, DPR, rotate, mobile) in the browser pane; the AGENT can set the viewport (width/height/aspect ratio/DPR/mobile) and can spawn standalone browser windows at an exact size, aspect ratio and DPR. Codex lessons to copy or avoid: Codex has a Dimensions toolbar with Responsive/Laptop/phone presets and a Browser Use viewport API. Its iPhone preset changes viewport and DPR but NOT the HTTP User-Agent (openai/codex#35576), so SSR pages render the desktop variant; we must switch viewport, DPR, touch AND User-Agent (+ client hints) together. Its agent-set viewport/toolbar gets lost when the agent releases control (openai/codex#35756, #34335); ours must persist until the user resets it and show a visible badge. Repo conventions: TypeScript, small pure helpers in src/shared with vitest tests, comments only where the surrounding code has them, no new dependencies. Verification for every code node: `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` pass. Do not weaken existing tests.
T01_spike_emulation.report:
## Outcome
docs/RESPONSIVE_BROWSER.md written with measured yes/no for a-f, chosen mechanisms, ViewportSpec, presets, limits, ordered interface list. Harness kept at scripts/responsive-spike.mjs. No product code changed.

## Facts Learned
- Metrics override persists across nav, reload, cross-origin, DevTools open/close, renderer crash+reload (a: yes).
- UA override changes HTTP UA on all navs, but Electron 44 sends NO Sec-CH-UA* headers at all; injecting via session.webRequest.onBeforeSendHeaders (by webContentsId) works (b).
- Fit: use `scale` in setDeviceMetricsOverride with native view sized w*scale; OS input and picker correct. Without scale the viewport is unreachable. CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent coords are in scaled view px when scale!=1 (x=125 -> clientX 250 at 0.5) -- contradicts plan premise; multiply by scale.
- captureScreenshot gives emulated size x DPR (390x600 at 1/2/3 -> 390, 780, 1170 wide); hangs when the window is minimized; works hidden; first capture after metrics change while hidden may be stale.
- openDevTools detach coexists with debugger (e).
- Detached window: showInactive does not steal focus; DPR/screen/touch are the display's, so must be emulated; CDP input/screenshots work unfocused; windows clamp to work area (393x852 -> 375x813).
- mobile:true without viewport meta yields 980px layout viewport (expected).

## Decisions Made
Scale-to-fit; UA profile + client-hint hook + touch together; viewport persists in BrowserManager per tab with agent badge; limits 200..3840, dpr 1..4, 4 agent windows/session; no approval for viewport changes; large windows satisfied by emulation + smaller native window.

## Files Touched
docs/RESPONSIVE_BROWSER.md, scripts/responsive-spike.mjs

## Interfaces Changed
None (proposed list in the doc).

## Verification
Ran `node_modules/.bin/electron scripts/responsive-spike.mjs` several times, numbers recorded in doc. No TS changed; typecheck/test not affected.

## Risks
setEmitTouchEventsForMouse not verified to emit touch events. Stale first capture while hidden. Header hook must be keyed per webContents.

## Recommended Next Step
Implement shared pure helpers (ViewportSpec, presets, UA profiles, clamp, fitScale, input coord conversion) with vitest tests; account for the flagged contradictions (input scale, client-hint hook, window clamp).

T02_viewport_model.title: Add the shared viewport model with presets, resolution and fit math
T02_viewport_model.instruction:
Goal: the pure, tested core of the feature, shared by main, renderer and the pi extension.

Follow docs/RESPONSIVE_BROWSER.md (from T01_spike_emulation) for the shapes and limits.

Steps:
1. Create src/shared/viewport.ts exporting: ViewportSpec (resolved: width, height, dpr, mobile, userAgent profile id, label, source 'user' | 'agent'), DEVICE_PRESETS, and a resolveViewport(request) that accepts any of: preset id; width and/or height; aspect ('9:19.5' or '16/9' or a number) combined with one known edge; dpr; mobile; orientation ('portrait'|'landscape' swaps edges). It validates and clamps to the documented limits, rounds to integers, and throws readable errors the agent can act on (for example 'aspect needs width or height').
2. Add fitViewport(pane: {width,height}, spec, opts) returning the native view bounds (centered) and the scale factor (<=1 unless the user chose zoom), following the mechanism chosen in T01.
3. Add userAgentFor(profile) that returns the UA string and client-hint metadata for mobile/tablet profiles, derived from the running Chromium version passed in as an argument (do not hardcode a stale version).
4. Extend BrowserTab in src/shared/browser.ts with optional `viewport?: ViewportSpec` and `surface?: 'pane' | 'window'` (type only; later nodes fill them).
5. Add src/shared/viewport.test.ts: preset lookup, aspect + edge resolution, orientation swap, clamping and error messages, fit math (smaller, larger, extreme aspect ratios), UA profile output.

Deliverables: src/shared/viewport.ts, src/shared/viewport.test.ts, small type additions in src/shared/browser.ts.

Acceptance: pnpm typecheck and pnpm test pass; the module has no Electron or DOM imports.

T02_viewport_model.report:
## Outcome
src/shared/viewport.ts (pure, no Electron/DOM) with tests; BrowserTab gained optional `viewport` and `surface`. typecheck and test pass.

## Facts Learned
Added tests all pass (356 total tests, 40 files).

## Decisions Made
- Module is src/shared/viewport.ts (not browser.ts as the doc proposed); ViewportSpec = {width,height,dpr,mobile,touch,userAgent (UaProfileId),label,source}. `touch` kept from the doc.
- resolveViewport: missing edge falls back to preset or 1280x800; aspect needs exactly one edge; orientation applied after aspect; mobile on a custom size picks iphone (<600 wide) else ipad; mobile:false forces native UA. Label stays preset label only if unmodified, else "Custom".
- fitViewport(pane, spec, {zoom}) -> {bounds (centred, relative to pane), scale}; scale=min(1,...) min 0.01; zoom honoured as is.
- userAgentFor(profile, chromiumVersion) -> {userAgent, platform, metadata (userAgentMetadata), headers (Sec-CH-UA, -Mobile, -Platform)} or null for native; iOS UAs use CriOS/<major>.0.0.0, Android uses Chrome/<major>.0.0.0.
- toInputCoords(x,y,scale) included for the CDP input scale finding.

## Files Touched
src/shared/viewport.ts, src/shared/viewport.test.ts, src/shared/browser.ts (type import + two optional fields)

## Interfaces Changed
New exports: ViewportSpec, ViewportRequest, DevicePreset, UaProfileId, VIEWPORT_LIMITS, DEVICE_PRESETS, findPreset, parseAspect, resolveViewport, rotateViewport, fitViewport, toInputCoords, userAgentFor. BrowserTab.viewport?, BrowserTab.surface?.

## Verification
pnpm typecheck: clean. pnpm test: 40 files, 356 tests passed.

## Risks
Preset IDs/labels are my choice (laptop, desktop, iphone-15, iphone-se, pixel-8, ipad). Pixel/UA strings are fixed (iOS 18, Android 14). Later nodes must import from ./viewport (UaProfileId not in browser.ts).

## Recommended Next Step
Main-side applyViewport using fitViewport/userAgentFor(process.versions.chrome) and the per-session header hook.

T03_manager_emulation.title: Apply per-tab viewport emulation in BrowserManager and expose IPC
T03_manager_emulation.instruction:
Goal: BrowserManager owns each tab's viewport and applies it through CDP, so user and agent both go through one path.

Steps:
1. Move the lazy debugger attach/cdp() helper out of src/main/browser/agent.ts into the manager (or a small shared module in src/main/browser/) so manager and agent use the same attached session. Keep agent behavior unchanged.
2. Add Tab.viewport (ViewportSpec | undefined) and a manager method setViewport(id, spec | undefined) that applies or clears Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride, Emulation.setUserAgentOverride (+ metadata), Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled exactly as decided in docs/RESPONSIVE_BROWSER.md, then reloads the page when the UA changed so the next request carries the new UA. Re-apply after render-process-gone recovery and whenever T01 found it can be lost; clear everything on reset (back to the real UA and metrics).
3. Make applyLayout() compute the native view bounds with fitViewport() from src/shared/viewport.ts instead of always filling the pane rect, keeping the existing app-zoom scaling and the detach rules.
4. Include viewport in snapshot() so BrowserState tabs carry it; the viewport survives navigation and tab switches until reset or the tab closes, whoever set it.
5. Add IPC channel browserViewport in src/shared/ipc.ts, handle it in src/main/index.ts with the existing trusted-sender wrapper, and expose browser().viewport(id, request) in src/preload/index.ts (the request goes through resolveViewport; reject invalid input without crashing). Update the window.studio type if it is declared separately.

Deliverables: updated manager.ts, the relocated cdp helper, ipc.ts, preload, main/index.ts.

Acceptance: pnpm typecheck and pnpm test pass; with a dev run, calling the IPC with a phone preset makes a loaded fixture page report the emulated innerWidth/dpr/UA and an HTTP server sees the mobile UA; resetting restores the real values.

T03_manager_emulation.report:
## Outcome
BrowserManager owns per-tab viewport emulation via CDP; IPC browser:viewport exposed. typecheck and tests pass. Not verified in a live dev run (no Electron run done this turn).
## Facts Learned
log.warn exists; Electron session.webRequest.onBeforeSendHeaders is a single hook per session, so it is registered once in the BrowserManager constructor.
## Decisions Made
- cdp() moved to src/main/browser/cdp.ts, used by agent.ts and manager.ts (agent behaviour unchanged).
- Manager.setViewport(id, ViewportRequest|undefined) resolves via resolveViewport, applies metrics (scale = fitViewport scale), touch, emitTouchEventsForMouse, UA+metadata, and client-hint headers via a Map<webContentsId, headers>; reloads if UA profile changed. Reset clears all and removes headers.
- Re-apply on render-process-gone and debugger detach; applyLayout re-sends metrics when fit scale changes (Tab.emulatedScale) and on activation.
- IPC handler forces source "user"; agent will call manager.setViewport directly with source "agent". Invalid input rejects the invoke (non-object throws; resolveViewport errors propagate).
## Files Touched
src/main/browser/cdp.ts (new), manager.ts, agent.ts, src/shared/ipc.ts, src/preload/index.ts, src/main/index.ts
## Interfaces Changed
IPC.browserViewport; BrowserApi.viewport(id, request|null): Promise<ViewportSpec|null>; BrowserManager.setViewport; Tab.viewport/emulatedScale; BrowserState tabs carry viewport.
## Verification
pnpm typecheck clean; pnpm test all pass.
## Risks
Live behaviour (UA reaching server, reset) rests on spike measurements, not re-run. Agent input coords still need toInputCoords with tab.emulatedScale (agent node). Metrics sent while pane is hidden use viewport size as the pane (scale 1) until layout arrives.
## Recommended Next Step
Agent viewport actions (use manager.setViewport with source agent, input scale from tab.emulatedScale) and the renderer Dimensions toolbar.

T04_agent_viewport_tool.title: Add the browser_viewport agent tool and viewport-aware screenshots
T04_agent_viewport_tool.instruction:
Goal: let the agent set, read and reset the viewport of its tab, and make every result tell it which viewport it is looking at.

Steps:
1. Extend AgentAction/AgentResult in src/shared/browser.ts with a `viewport` action: { action: 'viewport', set?: {preset?, width?, height?, aspect?, dpr?, mobile?, orientation?}, reset?: boolean } returning the resolved ViewportSpec; add the action name to the ACTIONS set in src/main/browser/agent.ts and implement it with ensureVisible(tab), resolveViewport(), manager.setViewport(); source is 'agent'.
2. Register `browser_viewport` in resources/browser-extension.ts with a typebox schema and a description that lists the preset ids, explains aspect/dpr/mobile/orientation, and says it persists until reset. No approval prompt (it is not a navigation); keep the ABOUT prefix style. Add `viewport` info to the shared reply text.
3. Add a one-line 'Viewport: 393x852 @3x, mobile, iPhone 15 (set by you|the user)' header to browser_snapshot output and to browser_screenshot's text, so a viewport the user changed is visible to the agent; omit it when no emulation is active.
4. Make browser_screenshot correct under emulation: Page.captureScreenshot is already emulated, but cap the long edge (e.g. 1600px) instead of only width 1280 so tall phone shots are not squashed, and report the emulated CSS size and DPR in the text.
5. Add the tool-call labels ('Set viewport' / 'Reset viewport' with target like '393x852 @3x') in src/renderer/src/lib/tools.ts.

Deliverables: shared types, agent.ts, browser-extension.ts, tools.ts.

Acceptance: pnpm typecheck and pnpm test pass; a browser.test.ts or new test covers the extension-side argument shaping if it is pure; manual check through the running app: browser_viewport {preset:'iphone-15'} then browser_screenshot returns a portrait image and snapshot shows the Viewport header; {reset:true} clears it.

T05_pane_dimensions_toolbar.title: Build the Dimensions toolbar and device frame in the browser pane
T05_pane_dimensions_toolbar.instruction:
Goal: the user-facing responsive mode in BrowserPane, equivalent to Codex's Dimensions toolbar.

Steps:
1. In src/renderer/src/components/BrowserPane.tsx add a toggle button (lucide icon such as Smartphone/MonitorSmartphone) in the address toolbar that shows a second row, the Dimensions toolbar, for the active tab: a preset dropdown (Responsive, the presets from src/shared/viewport.ts, Custom), width and height number inputs, a DPR select (1, 2, 3 and custom), a rotate button, a mobile/touch toggle, a zoom/fit indicator ('Fit 63%'), and a Reset button. All changes call browser().viewport(tab.id, request).
2. The toolbar reads tab.viewport from BrowserState so it reflects changes made by the agent: show a small 'Set by pi' badge when source is 'agent', and keep the row pinned (visible) whenever a viewport is active, even if the user never opened it, so an agent-set viewport can never be lost or hidden.
3. Draw the stage: the existing viewport div becomes a letterboxed stage with a subtle device frame/ruler labels (width x height) around the native view bounds computed by fitViewport (reuse the same function as main so DOM and native view agree); the layout reporter in the useLayoutEffect must report the same pane rect as today, main does the fitting.
4. Keep existing behaviors: the native view hides when the DOM overlay conditions are true (suggestions, lightbox, overlays), the annotation bar, full/split view and sidebar-width re-reporting. Persist the toolbar open/closed preference only if the existing pane state pattern already persists similar flags.

Deliverables: BrowserPane.tsx (extract a DimensionsBar component if the file gets unwieldy), any small state additions in src/renderer/src/state/app.ts.

Acceptance: pnpm typecheck and pnpm test pass; in `pnpm dev` the user can pick iPhone 15, see the page re-render at 393x852 centered with a frame, rotate, change DPR, and Reset; no DOM overlap with the native view at any pane width.

T06_window_surfaces.title: Support standalone browser windows with exact size, aspect ratio and DPR
T06_window_surfaces.instruction:
Goal: a tab can live in its own BrowserWindow whose content size is exactly what was asked, instead of the dragged pane.

Follow docs/RESPONSIVE_BROWSER.md for the window mechanics measured in T01.

Steps:
1. Add Tab.surface ('pane' | window id) in src/main/browser/manager.ts. Extract the view attach/detach/bounds logic so it works for a target contentView (the app window or a device window) rather than only this.window.
2. Implement openWindow(spec: ViewportSpec, url?, agent?) creating a BrowserWindow with useContentSize at spec.width x spec.height (in DIPs), setAspectRatio when the user may resize, showInactive so it never steals focus, a title showing the label and size, no menu bar, and the same partition/webPreferences hardening as pane tabs. The tab's WebContentsView fills the window; DPR/mobile/UA emulation reuses setViewport from T03 so the device pixel ratio is emulated rather than the display's.
3. Add popOut(tabId) (move an existing pane tab into a window sized to its current viewport or the pane size) and returnToPane(tabId). Decision: closing a window closes its tab; 'Return to pane' is the explicit way back; document this in docs/RESPONSIVE_BROWSER.md.
4. Lifecycle: closeTab/destroy close windows; closing a window removes its tab and emits state; windows are closed when the app window closes; a per-session cap (4) is enforced with a clear error.
5. BrowserState tabs carry `surface`; the pane tab strip data must still list window tabs (flagged) so the user can find them. ensureVisible() must NOT reveal the pane for a tab that lives in a window.
6. IPC: browserPopOut / browserReturn channels in ipc.ts, main/index.ts, preload.

Deliverables: manager.ts changes, IPC wiring.

Acceptance: pnpm typecheck and pnpm test pass; in a dev run a 390x844 @3 window opens without taking focus, a fixture page inside reports innerWidth 390 and devicePixelRatio 3, and closing it cleans up the tab and state.

## Outcome
BrowserManager supports tabs living in standalone BrowserWindows: openWindow, popOut, returnToPane, focusWindow, cap of 4, lifecycle cleanup, IPC wiring. typecheck and tests pass. NOT verified in a live dev run (no Electron launch this turn), so the 390x844@3 acceptance check (innerWidth/devicePixelRatio, no focus steal, cleanup) is untested live; it rests on T01 spike measurements.
## Facts Learned
getContentSize returns number[] (noUncheckedIndexedAccess needs defaults).
## Decisions Made
- Tab.surface: "pane" | window id, plus Tab.win. activeId = addressed tab (may be a window tab); new paneId = the tab drawn in the pane. applyLayout uses paneId only.
- Window: useContentSize at spec size, setAspectRatio(w/h), showInactive after emulation is applied, removeMenu, hardened webPreferences; view fill/fit via layoutWindow (re-emulates scale on resize/OS clamp).
- Closing a window closes its tab; returnToPane is the explicit way back (documented). popOut of a viewport-less tab invents a viewport (autoViewport) dropped on return.
- ensureVisible for window tabs never reveals the pane; restores a minimized window.
- App window "close" closes all device windows. 5th window throws a clear error.
- IPC browserActivate also raises a window tab (user click).
## Files Touched
src/main/browser/manager.ts, src/main/index.ts, src/shared/ipc.ts, src/preload/index.ts, docs/RESPONSIVE_BROWSER.md
## Interfaces Changed
BrowserManager.openWindow(request, url?, agent?): Promise<Tab>, popOut(id), returnToPane(id), focusWindow(id), WINDOW_LIMIT; IPC.browserPopOut/browserReturn; BrowserApi.popOut/returnToPane; BrowserState tabs carry surface.
## Verification
pnpm typecheck clean; pnpm test 359 passed.
## Risks
Live behaviour unverified. Renderer tab strip does not yet flag window tabs or offer pop-out/return buttons. Agent window action not yet wired to openWindow (return actual window size vs emulated size still to do).
## Recommended Next Step
Wire agent `window` actions to openWindow (report actual content size), UI pop-out/return controls + window flag in tab strip, then a live dev run of the acceptance check.

1. 5. Clean up: when the session that spawned windows closes (find how session-host.ts and the bridge map handles to sessions), close its windows.

browser_window tool (open/close/list) added and wired to manager.openWindow; all other browser_* tools accept an optional `tab` id. T09_verify_real_surface.report:
## Outcome
Added scripts/verify-responsive-browser.mjs (+ `pnpm verify:responsive`). It runs the real built app against a local fixture server and passes 20/20 checks after a fresh `pnpm build`. Running it found and fixed two defects from earlier nodes (below). pnpm typecheck clean; pnpm test 359 passed.

## Facts Learned
- Real bug (T07): calling Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride on a WebContentsView that never navigated SEGVs the whole Electron 44.5.1 main process on macOS (null deref; confirmed by bisecting with logs in out/main/index.js). browser_window open with no prior load hit it every time.
- Real bug (T04): agent `viewport set` passed an already-resolved spec back into setViewport, which re-resolved it with explicit width/height, so presets were labelled "Custom" instead of e.g. "iPhone 15".
- The app hands its bridge address+token to the pi child via PIGNA_BRIDGE/PIGNA_TOKEN, so the script uses a wrapper PIGNA_PI_BIN that records them and then runs fake-pi; the script then POSTs /browser like the extension does. Main-process state (window sizes, focus) is read over `--inspect`.
- In a running app the pane tab got 526x758 @2x as its native viewport; reset restores exactly that.
- setAspectRatio was NOT the crash (I first suspected it); it is retained.

## Decisions Made
- Fix the crash centrally in BrowserManager.emulate: a view without a URL loads about:blank before metrics are sent (covers windows and blank pane tabs).
- Agent now passes the raw request (+source "agent") to setViewport; validation still throws the same errors.
- Added package.json `verify:responsive` since siblings (release, icon, build:computer-use) have entries.

## Files Touched
scripts/verify-responsive-browser.mjs (new), package.json, src/main/browser/manager.ts, src/main/browser/agent.ts

## Interfaces Changed
None (script `verify:responsive` added).

## Verification
Commands: `pnpm build`; `pnpm verify:responsive`; `pnpm typecheck`; `pnpm test`.
Output of the final run (all PASS): native 526x758@2x; iphone-15 result label "iPhone 15" 393x852@3x; page sees 393x852@3x, coarse pointer, iPhone UA; server saw iPhone/Mobile UA with sec-ch-ua-mobile ?1 after the reload; page rendered MOBILE variant; viewport (393@3x, iPhone UA) survives navigation to /b; screenshot 738x1600 (cap 1600 of 1179x2556); 16:9 width 1280 dpr 2 -> 1280x720, page sees 1280x720@2x desktop UA; screenshot 1600x900; browser_window 360 aspect 9:16 dpr3 -> 360x640@3x, page sees same, window content size [360,640], did not take focus (isFocused false), screenshot 900x1600; close removes window; reset restores 526x758@2x, native UA, non-coarse pointer. "all 20 checks passed".

## Risks
- Script uses PIGNA_BACKGROUND and ports 9478/9479 (fixed); fails if those are busy. Window focus check is meaningful only because the app runs in background mode.
- Pane screenshots rely on the pane being laid out; at the test app size (526x758) the iphone-15 emulation fit scale is <1 yet screenshots were still full size, but agent click coordinates under fit scale <1 are still unverified.
- The UI Dimensions bar, pop-out/return and badge (T08 and earlier user UI nodes) are not covered by this script; it drives the bridge only.
- Blank tab now loads about:blank when emulated, so the URL bar of an empty tab can show about:blank.

## Recommended Next Step
Add a click-through check (agent `click` under fit scale <1) and a renderer-driven check of the Dimensions bar / pop-out via scripts/cdp.mjs.
